source_text:
Φίλωνα καὶ Ῥέον Ἀγαθόπουν, οἳ ἐπηκολούθησάν μοι εἰς λόγον θεοῦ, καλῶς ἐποιήσατε ὑποδεξάμενοι ὡς διακόνους θεοῦ: οἳ καὶ εὐχαριστοῦσιν τῷ κυρίῳ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὺς ἀνεπαύσατε κατὰ πάντα τρόπον. οὐδὲν ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ ἀπολεῖται.
ἀντίψυχον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμά μου καὶ τὰ δεσμά μου, ἃ οὐχ ὑπερηφανήσατε οὐδὲ ἐπῃσχύνθητε. οὐδὲ ὑμᾶς ἐπαισχυνθήσεται ἡ τελεία ἐλπίς, Ἰησοῦς Χριστός.
thought_title: Thanks for receiving Philo and Rheus Agathopus
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Smyrnaeans, thanking them for receiving two companions who followed him for the sake of God's word.
pass_a_gloss: Philo and Rheus Agathopus, who followed me for the sake of the word of God, you did well in receiving as deacons of God; who also give thanks to the Lord on your behalf, because you refreshed them in every way. Nothing for you will by no means be lost. My spirit and my bonds are a ransom for you, which you did not despise nor were ashamed of. Nor will the perfect hope, Jesus Christ, be ashamed of you.

choices.english: for the sake of the word of God
choices.why: The prepositional phrase indicates purpose or cause; 'for the sake of' captures the sense that they followed Ignatius because of God's word.
The glossary requires 'deacon' for διάκονος; 'of God' preserves the genitive θεοῦ.
The noun means a life given in exchange for another; 'ransom' conveys the substitutionary sense.
The adjective τελεία modifies ἐλπίς; 'perfect' is the standard rendering and matches the theological weight Ignatius gives to Christ as hope.

choices.english: will by no means be lost
choices.why: The double negative οὐ μή with the future indicative expresses emphatic negation; 'by no means' preserves the force.

pass_b_english: You did well to receive Philo and Rheus Agathopus as deacons of God. They followed me for the sake of the word of God, and they give thanks to the Lord for you, because you refreshed them in every way. Nothing will be lost to you at all.
My spirit is a ransom for you, and my bonds as well, which you did not despise or feel ashamed of. Nor will the perfect hope, Jesus Christ, be ashamed of you.

problems.quote: Nothing you have done will by any means be lost
problems.why: Double negative οὐ...οὐ μὴ is emphatic future denial: 'nothing will be lost to you.' English 'Nothing...will...be lost' loses the emphatic 'by any means' nuance but keeps sense. However, 'you have done' adds unstated content.
problems.fix: Nothing will by any means be lost to you
problems.ruling: οὐδὲν ὑμῖν means 'nothing to/for you'; 'you have done' adds unstated content not in source.

edits.old: Nothing you have done will by any means be lost.
edits.new: Nothing will by any means be lost to you.

problems.quote: May my spirit be a ransom for you
problems.why: Source is declarative, not optative; 'May...be' turns statement into wish, changing force.
problems.fix: My spirit is a ransom for you
problems.ruling: ἀντίψυχον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμά μου is declarative, not optative; 'May...be' changes statement to wish.

edits.old: May my spirit be a ransom for you, and my bonds as well,
edits.new: My spirit is a ransom for you, and my bonds as well,

fixed: Changed 'May my spirit be a ransom for you' to declarative 'My spirit is a ransom for you' to match the source's indicative force.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'Eucharist' for εὐχαριστία, but this is the verb εὐχαριστέω, not the noun.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐχαριστοῦσιν is verb εὐχαριστέω; 'give thanks' is correct. No glossary issue in this text.

last_rejected.why: 'Ransom' suggests payment; ἀντίψυχον means 'life given in exchange/soul for soul'.
last_rejected.fix: my spirit is given in exchange for you
last_rejected.ruling: ἀντίψυχον means 'ransom/price of a life'; 'ransom' is standard rendering, not wrong.

last_rejected.why: ὑπερηφανέω means 'treat with haughty disdain/scorn,' not merely 'despise.'
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπερηφανέω means 'despise/scorn'; 'despise' is within normal range, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified the relationship between the clauses so the deacons' identity and their thanksgiving flow naturally, and made the pronoun references explicit for a modern reader.

notes.why: The name appears as 'Rheus Agathopus' (full name) and likely 'Agathopus' alone; but also check if 'Rheus' is a separate name or title. Actually in 6.10 it's 'Rheus Agathopus' again. No drift found—false flag.
